author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice extends the vet feature package along its existing shape: a declarative Spring Data read, a controller that calls the repository directly, and a Thymeleaf page. No new package, type, or layer. Two decisions are new ground and are now recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-18-specialty-narrowed-veterinarian-read.md with rules in system-design.md Contracts. First, the narrowed read is not cached: both existing VetRepository reads carry @Cacheable("vets"), the vets cache has no eviction and no size bound, and every route is unauthenticated, so a caller-supplied key would be an unbounded attacker-controlled key space. Second, case-insensitive matching is expressed in the query, not left to the column collation, which is how the confirmed PostgreSQL owner-search defect arose. The narrowed read is a new read method beside the two existing ones; the controller keeps calling the cached unnarrowed reads when no specialty is given.
integration_points: VetRepository gains a paged and an unpaged read narrowed by specialty name, traversing the existing Vet.specialties ManyToMany into Specialty.name; neither carries @Cacheable
VetController.showVetList and showResourcesVetList each accept an optional specialty request parameter and branch to the narrowed read only when the value is non-blank
the vet list template's paging block carries the specialty on every page link, so totalPages and currentPage stay consistent with the narrowed result
no new user-facing text: the template gains no label, so the eleven message bundles and the bundle-parity test are untouched

patterns.description: declarative derived query returning Page<T> with a Pageable — the shape the narrowed vet reads follow; Spring Data derives the join from the nested property path
blank search input is normalized in the controller before the repository call, not inside the query — put the blank-specialty normalization in the same place
the existing paging block; page links are built today by string preprocessing, which must not be reused for a caller-supplied value (see risks)
the two rules governing the narrowed read, both back-linked to the new ADR

risks.risk: copying @Cacheable("vets") onto the narrowed read, matching its two siblings — the obvious pattern-following move
risks.mitigation: leave the narrowed reads unannotated; the vets cache has no eviction or size bound and every route is unauthenticated, so a caller-supplied cache key grows memory without limit (ADR 2026-08-18-specialty-narrowed-veterinarian-read)

risks.risk: building page links by string preprocessing, e.g. @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__&specialty=__${specialty}__'} — this reflects a caller-controlled string into an href without URL encoding
risks.mitigation: use Thymeleaf's link parameter syntax, @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes each value and omits a null parameter

risks.risk: reaching case-insensitivity through the column collation reproduces the confirmed PostgreSQL owner-search defect — the same request would return different results per vendor
risks.mitigation: express the case fold in the query itself (derived-query IgnoreCase keyword or an explicit lower() comparison), so H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL agree and the H2-backed suite is evidence for all three

risks.risk: the join into vet_specialties can multiply rows, corrupting the page count and the totalItems the page shows
risks.mitigation: use a distinct read and assert the narrowed page count in a test, not only the row contents

risks.risk: handling the blank value inside the query (a predicate that treats an empty string as match-all) makes blank a distinct execution path from absent, which the acceptance criteria say must be identical
risks.mitigation: normalize in the controller: a null, empty, or whitespace-only value takes the existing unnarrowed, cached read unchanged

risks.risk: the machine-readable surface is unpaged today and the prd-entry lists paging it as a non-goal; adding a Pageable there would exceed scope
risks.mitigation: the narrowed unpaged read returns the whole matching collection into the Vets wrapper, mirroring the current unnarrowed behavior

notes: Durable memory updated by this dispatch. docs/system-design.md: Contracts Implements now cite REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004 on Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, and VetController (Vets moves off the em-dash, since the machine-readable document is now a supported surface); a new Contracts paragraph carries the two rules with ADR back-links; a Threat Model row records unbounded cache growth from caller-supplied read parameters; Open Question 5 notes that the absent size bound is the same gap; the Known Defects row claiming the machine-readable vet route serves no requirement was removed, since REQ-VET-003 now covers that surface. docs/adr/2026-08-18-specialty-narrowed-veterinarian-read.md is new. docs/adr/README.md gained index rows for that ADR and for the product expert's non-goal ADR — the item the prd-entry notes flagged as outside its write scope is now closed. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. The three open questions the product expert recorded (a visible specialty control, paging the machine-readable directory, narrowing to several specialties at once) need no design position now; each would be a fresh slice.
